submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad layer-0 previous-token head that is weakly to moderately active on most ordinary prose (typical sentence peaks 0.8-1.8, above the ~0.75 active line) and peaks maximally narrowly at 'of' completing 'one of' (~3.0; other quantifier/nominal-plus-'of' such as 'two of' peak 1.6-2.4 and modifier-noun pairs such as 'closed doors' peak ~1.8), and it falls back to its floor only when every measured token is drawn from a closed bleached-sink set -- 'of', 'to', the be-forms is/are/was/were/be/being/been, and the core prepositions in/on/at/for/with/by -- whether as homogeneous runs ('of'x8 peaks 0.0, 'was'x8 peaks 0.0, 'be'x8 peaks 0.05) or as mixed cycles inside that set ('of to is in' peaks 0.0, 'is are was were be being been' peaks 0.0, 'in on at for with by' peaks 0.0, 'is was of' repeats peak 0.0, all with a terminal '.' still <=0.03), with the same peak token collapsing from 3.0 to 0.58 when its predecessor changes from 'one' to the sink copula 'was'. Crucially, any token outside that set breaks the floor: heterogeneous copula chains ('is seem seemed remain become became' peaks 1.83), heterogeneous preposition chains ('from over under...' peaks 0.97, 'pending barring...' peaks 2.15), determiner mixes ('a an the this...' peaks 1.2), and homogeneous runs of non-sink tokens ('and'x8 peaks 1.76, 'the'x8 peaks 1.13, 'one'x8 peaks 2.93, '.'x8 peaks 1.98) all ride above the line.

rival_explanations: Every 'X of' bigram peaks near-maximally regardless of X, so stranded 'of' after a verb or copula ('She saw was of the horses') peaks as strongly as 'one of'.

Only the exact bigram 'one of' (and proper-name-plus-period such as 'Mrs.') drives the head; other quantifier-'of' bigrams ('two of', 'each of', 'most of') and modifier-noun pairs ('closed doors') stay below the active line.
